outcome: Obstetric lesions of the anal sphincter (OASIS)
cohort: The study included 464 parturient patients admitted to the AOU Maggiore della Carita, Novara, Italy, who delivered between 2013 and 2023.
finding: The incidence of OASIS was 1.1%, with significant risk factors including nulliparity, previous caesarean sections, assisted reproduction technology, induced delivery, use of oxytocin, epidural analgesia, prolonged gestation, position at delivery, prolonged labor, vacuum cup application, and newborn size.
mod_finding: Induced delivery, use of oxytocin for augmentation, epidural analgesia, position at delivery, duration of labor, and application of a vacuum cup were found to be significant risk factors for OASIS.
birth_weight: Newborn weight was measured as a risk factor; no specific weight range for inclusion in the study was mentioned.
gest_age: Delivery after 40 weeks of gestation was measured as a risk factor; no specific gestational age range for inclusion in the study was mentioned.
